pll1d15c4-d1e3477.summary: Cites Ambrose: since the prophet did not specify by whom the Son was given, he was given by the grace of the Trinity, so the Son gave himself. If given by himself, he was sent and proceeded from himself, which must be granted since his mission is a divine work.
claims: The Son was given by the Trinity, including himself.
The Son was sent by himself.
The Son's mission is a divine work.

pll1d15c4-d1e3488.summary: Cites De Trinitate II: the Son was sent also by himself because Mary's conception and birth were the Trinity's work. As the Father sanctified him and he sanctified himself, and the Father handed him over and he handed himself over, there is one will and inseparable operation. The incarnation in which he was sent was done by Father and Son, with the Spirit. He was not sent by changing place, being already in the world. Had the Word turned into a visible creature, he would be only sent and not also sender, but since he took the form of a servant while remaining unchangeably in the form of God, the invisible Father with the invisible Son made the Son visible.
claims: The incarnation is the inseparable work of Father, Son, and Spirit.
The Son sanctified and handed himself over, as did the Father.
The Son was not sent by change of place.
The Son was sender as well as sent because the Word was not changed into a creature.

pll1d15c4-d1e3543.summary: Concludes that the Son was sent by the Father, by the Spirit, and by himself, and that the mission is the incarnation, his being made man and appearing visibly, the common work of the three.
claims: The Son was sent by Father, Spirit, and himself.
The Son's mission is the incarnation.
The incarnation is the common work of the three persons.

pl-l1d15c4.summary: Shows that the Son was also given and sent by himself. Ambrose: since Isaiah does not say by whom the Son was given, he was given by the grace of the Trinity, so also by himself. Augustine, De Trinitate II: the conception and birth from Mary is a work of the Trinity. As the Son was sanctified by the Father and sanctified himself, and was handed over by the Father and handed himself over, so the one will and inseparable work of Father and Son (with the Spirit) made the incarnation in which he was sent. He was not sent by change of place, since he was already in the world, and he was not changed into a creature but took the form of a servant while remaining in the form of God. So the mission of the Son is the incarnation, the common work of the three.
claims: The Son was given and sent by the Trinity, including himself.
The conception and birth from Mary is the work of the whole Trinity.
Father and Son have one will and inseparable operation.
The Son was not sent by change of place.
The Son took the form of a servant while remaining unchangeable in the form of God.
The Son's mission is the incarnation, a work common to the three persons.
